title: Deep links: universal links and URL schemes
summary: Deep links open a specific screen in your app from a URL. Universal links use normal https URLs verified by your website; custom URL schemes (`myapp://`) are simpler but anyone can claim them.
body: **In simple words:** A link like `https://shop.com/product/42` should open the product screen in the app if installed, and the website if not. That is a **universal link**.

**How universal links work:** (1) Add the Associated Domains capability `applinks:shop.com`. (2) Host an `apple-app-site-association` (AASA) JSON file at `https://shop.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` listing your app ID and which paths open the app. (3) iOS downloads it (via Apple's CDN) on install. (4) Tapping a matching link opens the app with an `NSUserActivity`.

**Custom URL schemes** (`shop://product/42`): declared in Info.plist; no verification, so another app could register the same scheme; and nothing happens if the app is not installed. Still used for app-to-app callbacks (e.g. OAuth redirects).

**Handling in the app:** SwiftUI `.onOpenURL` (schemes and universal links) or `onContinueUserActivity`; UIKit `scene(_:continue:)` and `scene(_:openURLContexts:)`. Parse the URL into a route and pass it to your router. If login is needed, store the route and continue after login.
**Deferred deep links:** link clicked before install → after install, open the right screen. Not built in; needs a server or attribution service to match.
**Testing:** links typed in Safari's address bar do not open the app; test from Notes/Messages. Validate the AASA file is served over https without redirects.
keyPoints: Universal links = https + AASA file + Associated Domains; secure and fall back to web.
URL schemes = easy but unverified and fail if app not installed.
Handle with `onOpenURL` / scene delegate; parse into routes; router navigates.
Queue the route if authentication is required.
Validate input from links - they come from outside.
mistakes: Trusting parameters from a deep link without validation (e.g. performing actions directly).
Serving the AASA file with redirects or the wrong content type.
followups: **Why might a universal link open Safari instead of the app?** AASA not reachable/cached, path not matched, user previously chose to open in Safari, or link opened from the same domain in Safari.
**How do you support marketing links that must work before install?** Deferred deep linking via a link service.
